title: Better Buy: Home Depot or Lowe's?
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; auto-captions garble names in places. Video was members-only in earlier runs and went public before this run; captions were fetched on a manual retry in this run after scan.py reported caption_ok:false (playability OK).
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc compares Home Depot and Lowe's through the post-COVID home-improvement hangover: revenue flat/low-single-digit expected in 2026, margins down (HD 15.5%->12.4%, LOW 15.5%->11.3%) on trade-barrier input costs and wages, but ROIC still above WACC (HD 18.5%, LOW 20%) and both at near-lowest-ever forward P/Es (HD ~18, LOW 14.3). DCFs: HD fair value $262 vs $291 market (fairly valued, within his 5-10% margin of safety); LOW fair value $230 vs $186 market (~24% upside, undervalued). He ranks BOTH as buying opportunities at current prices, with Lowe's the better buy. HD BUY and LOW BUY, both reiterated - no flips. (Video ends with a members-only Netflix earnings live plug for Tue 20 Oct.)

calls.thesis: Both HD and LOW ranked as buying opportunities at current prices; HD fairly valued (DCF $262 vs $291 market, within his 5-10% margin of safety), fwd P/E ~18 near its lowest ever, ROIC 18.5% still ~2x WACC despite margin fall 15.5%->12.4%. BUY reiterated (prior BUY 2026-10-03 @ $286) - no flip.
calls.base_case: Industry flat in 2026 (no/low single-digit growth), returning longer term to mid-to-high single-digit revenue growth.
calls.bull_case: Macro headwinds (except trade barriers) are temporary; hard-to-disrupt pro/heavy-goods model re-accelerates with the industry.
calls.bear_case: Near term (1-4 quarters) troublesome: flat revenue vs rising input/wage costs keeps margins falling.
